digest.definition: Law is studied as an academic subject joining legal knowledge, general intellectual skills and skills particular to law, with values and ethics in theory and practice
distinctiveFeatures: Law is studied as an academic subject joining legal knowledge, general intellectual skills and skills particular to law, with values and ethics in theory and practice
The degree alone does not license practice, though it prepares for regulated legal work; routes to qualification differ across the UK nations and are set by PSRBs
It borrows methods from the humanities and social sciences and attends to professional behaviours, well-being, the affective domain and citizenship
Its outlook is both national and global; a course may cover one jurisdiction or several
Law is treated as a system of power that can sustain or challenge inequality, so its study is critical and concerned with justice and fairness
Legal understanding is built through detailed work on substantive law, with no compulsory subjects set by the statement
Technology and artificial intelligence are changing legal services and the role of lawyers, and access to justice is a recurring concern
Practical and experiential learning, such as law clinics, public legal education, mooting and placements, sits alongside academic study
Graduates go into regulated practice and into many other skilled roles at home and abroad

themesInSubject.inThisSubject: law is read as a source of both inequality and challenge to it; courses bring out law and equality, aim for substantive equality in the curriculum and inclusive assessment and feedback, and students engage with debates on inequality (D1, 1.3, 1.6 to 1.8, 2.1, 3.5, 3.9, 3.12)

headed Sustainability in the text: law has a part in securing sustainable development; the SDGs and the UNESCO competencies are named, and students engage with debates on sustainability (D1, 1.3, 1.13, 1.14, 3.5, 4.4)

transferable.text: You will be able to think for yourself: ask and answer sharp questions, spot what you do not yet know and learn it, and analyse and evaluate critically.
You will be able to solve problems and adapt when things change.
You will be able to research independently: pin down the issue, find and judge reliable, up-to-date information from a wide range of sources and use it well.
You will be able to work with different kinds of data, such as text, numbers and statistics.
You will be able to communicate clearly and precisely, in speech or other ways, and respond with care to views different from your own.
You will be able to use digital tools to find, organise, create and share information.
You will be able to manage your own learning: reflect on it, act on feedback and advice, and own and correct your mistakes.
You will be willing and able to work well with others.
You will be able to take charge of your own personal and professional growth, including working with academic integrity.
You will be able to recognise ethical conflicts when they arise and resolve them through careful, balanced reasoning.
You will develop personal integrity and an awareness of the ethical effects your decisions can have.
You will develop the habit of professional reflection to improve how you work.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Law degree
Purposes and characteristics of a Law degree

statements.about: knowledge of the legal system or systems studied
statements.paraphrase: Law may be studied in one jurisdiction or several, with a national and a global outlook; whichever system or systems a course covers, the statement asks that students know its main features and principles. Coverage may take in relations among people, organisations and the state and the sources of law, and law's two-way link with ethical, social, political, environmental and economic norms may show in the curriculum.

forPractitioner.text: Whatever jurisdiction or jurisdictions the course covers, make sure students gain knowledge of that system's main features and principles; the statement requires this. Consider covering relations between persons, bodies and the state, the sources of law and how law shapes and is shaped by wider norms.

forBeneficiary.text: Whichever legal system or systems your course covers, you must come to know their main features and principles, which may include how people, organisations and the state relate in law and where law comes from.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Law degree

statements.about: law's interaction with equality, diversity and inclusion in the curriculum
statements.paraphrase: Because law regulates equality, diversity and inclusion and is tied to justice and fairness, courses will bring out how law interacts with these issues; study may prompt reflection on law's history, politics and effects here, including what legal understanding can and cannot do against systemic injustice.

forPractitioner.text: Bring the relationship between law and equality, diversity and inclusion to the fore in the curriculum, inviting students to reflect on the history, politics and effects of law in this area and on the reach and limits of legal tools for tackling systemic injustice.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a curriculum expectation on the course; the student meets it through what is taught

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Law degree

statements.about: widening access, inclusive methods and reasonable adjustments
statements.paraphrase: Providers show commitment to widening access and inclusive participation so every Law student can thrive whatever their background or disability; they plan ahead for inclusive teaching, learning and assessment aimed at access for marginalised groups, and will carry duties for reasonable adjustments and proactive prevention.

forPractitioner.text: Commit to widening access and inclusive participation, plan inclusive teaching, learning and assessment in advance with marginalised groups in mind, and meet your duties to make reasonable adjustments and to act preventively rather than only in response.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider; the student meets its effect in access and adjustments

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Law degree

statements.about: understanding disability in its many forms
statements.paraphrase: To meet disabled students' needs, inclusive learning environments could be built; disability in the context of studying law takes many forms and identities and should be understood in all of them, since disabled Law students may see their identities remade several times during their studies.

forPractitioner.text: Treat disability among Law students as many identities, not one, and understand it in all its forms; consider building inclusive learning environments, knowing that a disabled student's sense of identity may shift repeatedly through law school.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and its staff; the student meets its effect

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Law degree

statements.paraphrase: Providers need to consider flexible assessment methods so that different students' needs are met and learning can be shown in several ways.

forPractitioner.text: Consider flexibility in how students are assessed, so that varied needs are met and students can show their learning in more than one way.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider in designing assessment

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Law degree

statements.appliesTo: Law students across the honours degree
statements.about: progression across the levels towards the threshold
statements.paraphrase: Across an honours degree at FHEQ level 6 (FQHEIS level 10), students of Law will move from level to level under each institution's rules, with knowledge, skills, expertise and experience growing at each stage towards the threshold subject skills; this will usually mean completing and gaining credit for all learning and assessment, practical parts included. A graduate with a second-class degree or better would be expected to be ready for postgraduate study in Law or a related subject, though entry is for each provider to set.

forPractitioner.text: Plan each level so that knowledge, skills and experience build steadily towards the threshold subject skills by the end of the honours degree, with credit awarded for all learning and assessment, including practical work. Expect students with a second-class degree or better to be equipped for postgraduate study, while postgraduate entry rules remain your own.

forBeneficiary.text: As you move through each year of your honours degree you will build knowledge, skills and experience towards the minimum the subject sets for graduation, usually by passing all your learning and assessment, including any practical parts. With a second-class degree or better you would normally be ready for postgraduate study, though each course sets its own entry rules.

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Law degree

statements.appliesTo: students on combined, joint or major-minor routes
statements.paraphrase: Students on combined, joint or major-minor routes will reach the core of the subject's specific and generic skills and add others as their joint course requires; they may also study where their two subjects overlap.

forPractitioner.text: On joint, combined or major-minor routes, make sure students will reach the core subject-specific and generic Law skills, add the rest the partner subject requires and, where useful, offer interdisciplinary study of the overlap.

forBeneficiary.text: If you study Law with another subject, you will gain the core Law skills, both specific and general, and add others your joint course asks for; you may also explore where your two subjects meet.

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Law degree

statements.about: flexible, inclusive delivery and digital fluency
statements.paraphrase: Providers will look at a Law course's learning, teaching and assessment as a whole so that it offers creative learning across online, blended or in-person delivery, widens access and lets every student reach their potential in an inclusive, supportive setting; practical learning such as clinics, placements and mentoring can be considered in any mode, and digital tools will be used where suitable to build students' digital confidence and fluency, including knowing which technology suits a task.

forPractitioner.text: Design learning, teaching and assessment as a whole so the course works creatively across online, blended and face-to-face delivery, widens access and supports every student inclusively. Consider practical learning, such as clinical legal education, placements and mentoring, in any mode, and use digital tools where suitable to build students' digital confidence and fluency grounded in the discipline's values.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider in designing delivery; the student meets its effect

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Law degree

statements.paraphrase: Providers will try to use different technologies for flexible delivery that supports learning in accessible, meaningful and effective ways, opening fair access to knowledge exchange and skills, for instance through work-based, theoretical, skills-focused or graduate-entry routes.

forPractitioner.text: Look for technological means of flexible delivery that make learning accessible and meaningful, and consider offering varied routes, such as work-based, theoretical, skills-focused or graduate-entry courses, that widen fair access.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider in planning routes and delivery

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Law degree

statements.about: qualifying Law degrees and routes to professional qualification
statements.paraphrase: Qualifying Law degrees with professional and vocational outcomes will also need assessment and accreditation by the relevant PSRBs, and institutions should tell prospective and current students plainly which routes to professional qualification their courses offer.

forPractitioner.text: Where the course is a qualifying Law degree, secure the relevant PSRB accreditation, and be clear with applicants and current students about which professional qualification routes the course does and does not open.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the institution to inform students; the student is its audience, not its subject

statements.about: legal understanding through substantive law; awareness of PSRB requirements
statements.paraphrase: Law degrees give chances to build legal understanding: knowing, comprehending, questioning and applying the theories, concepts, values, rules and principles of public and private law across many contexts, recognising ambiguity and handling uncertainty, reaching evidenced conclusions on real or hypothetical problems, synthesising doctrine, policy and context, choosing reasoned solutions and judging arguments critically. No set subjects are required, but legal study is expected to engage in detail with substantive areas of law; courses may differ in content and jurisdiction, and providers designing a route into practice will know the relevant PSRB requirements.

forPractitioner.text: Give students the means to build legal understanding through detailed work on substantive areas of law of your choosing: questioning and applying the doctrine and theory of public and private law in varied contexts, handling ambiguity and uncertainty, reaching evidenced conclusions and weighing arguments. If the course is meant as a route into practice, take account of the relevant PSRB requirements.

forBeneficiary.text: Your course will help you build legal understanding by working in detail on real areas of law: you learn to question and apply legal ideas and rules in different settings, cope with uncertainty, reach conclusions backed by evidence and judge arguments. No particular law subjects are compulsory for this.

statements.paraphrase: Think independently: pose and answer sharp questions, spot and fill gaps in what they know, and analyse and evaluate critically.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will be equipped to think for themselves: to frame and answer pointed questions, notice and close gaps in their knowledge, and analyse and evaluate critically.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to think for yourself: ask and answer sharp questions, spot what you do not yet know and learn it, and analyse and evaluate critically.

statements.paraphrase: Solve problems and adapt to change.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will be equipped to solve problems and to adapt when circumstances change.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to solve problems and adapt when things change.

statements.about: independent research and use of information
statements.paraphrase: Carry out independent research well: identify the issues accurately, find, retrieve and evaluate accurate, current and relevant information from many suitable sources, and apply it properly.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will be equipped to research on their own: to pin down the issues, locate and judge reliable, up-to-date information from varied sources and use it appropriately.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to research independently: pin down the issue, find and judge reliable, up-to-date information from a wide range of sources and use it well.

statements.about: working with textual, numerical and statistical data
statements.paraphrase: Work with varied data, whether textual, numerical or statistical.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will be equipped to handle textual, numerical and statistical data.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to work with different kinds of data, such as text, numbers and statistics.

statements.about: clear communication responsive to other views
statements.paraphrase: Communicate clearly, effectively and precisely, in speech or other forms, responding fittingly and with sensitivity to differing views and arguments.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will be equipped to communicate precisely and effectively, verbally or otherwise, and to respond with care to positions they may not share.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to communicate clearly and precisely, in speech or other ways, and respond with care to views different from your own.

statements.paraphrase: Use digital skills to find, organise, create and share information.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will be equipped with digital literacy for locating, organising, producing and sharing information.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to use digital tools to find, organise, create and share information.

statements.paraphrase: Manage themselves: reflect on their learning, use feedback well, take advice and own and fix their mistakes.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will be equipped to manage their own learning, reflecting on it, acting on feedback and advice, and admitting and correcting errors.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to manage your own learning: reflect on it, act on feedback and advice, and own and correct your mistakes.

statements.paraphrase: Be willing and able to work with others.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will be equipped and willing to collaborate.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be willing and able to work well with others.

statements.about: personal and professional development and academic integrity
statements.paraphrase: Engage with their own personal and professional growth, academic integrity included.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will be equipped to take charge of their personal and professional development, including acting with academic integrity.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to take charge of your own personal and professional growth, including working with academic integrity.

statements.paraphrase: Understand ethical conflicts that may come up and how to settle them through reasoned, balanced judgement.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will be equipped to recognise ethical conflicts and resolve them by weighed, reasoned judgement.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to recognise ethical conflicts when they arise and resolve them through careful, balanced reasoning.

statements.about: integrity and ethical awareness in decisions
statements.paraphrase: Develop personal integrity and awareness of the ethical effects decisions may have.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will be equipped with personal integrity and an awareness of what their decisions may mean ethically.

forBeneficiary.text: You will develop personal integrity and an awareness of the ethical effects your decisions can have.

statements.paraphrase: Develop professional reflective capacity to improve their own practice.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will be equipped with professional reflective skills to improve their own practice.

forBeneficiary.text: You will develop the habit of professional reflection to improve how you work.

statements.about: inclusive, sustainable and accessible teaching; digital inclusivity
statements.paraphrase: Each provider's teaching and learning environment will reflect its own approach to legal study, with methods suited to the subject, the outcomes and learners' needs; innovation could shape the curriculum. Methods will take in sustainability, inclusion, diversity and accessibility, may mix live and recorded, technology-enhanced and in-person teaching, and providers will secure digital inclusivity as far as they can, such as fair access to Wi-Fi and devices.

forPractitioner.text: Choose teaching and learning methods that fit the material, the intended outcomes and your learners, and build in sustainability, inclusion, diversity and accessibility. Mix synchronous, asynchronous, technology-enhanced and classroom teaching as suits, and do what you can to secure equal digital access, such as Wi-Fi and equipment.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider in designing teaching

statements.about: staff development, learning resources and training in legal sources
statements.paraphrase: Teaching, research and professional practice interact in the Law learning environment. Staff will be given development opportunities and may hold or work towards a teaching qualification or recognition such as Advance HE's PSF. Students learn in a stimulating setting that welcomes intellectual and neurological diversity; they will have access to legal and academic sources, literature, databases, software and computing, will be trained to find and use legal sources, and will be supported to use these resources well, alone and in groups.

forPractitioner.text: Give staff development opportunities and support towards a teaching qualification or recognition such as the PSF. Make sure students can reach legal and academic sources, databases, software and computing, train them to identify, retrieve and use legal sources, and support them to use these resources in group and individual work.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider for staff and resources; the student meets its effect

statements.about: engagement with the legal community; awareness of professional bodies
statements.paraphrase: Legal education might engage actively with the legal and wider community; students may join legal projects inside or outside their provider, such as clinics, public legal education, outreach, research or placements, and will be told about relevant learned societies or professional bodies.

forPractitioner.text: Consider giving students chances to take part in legal projects within or beyond the institution, such as clinical or public legal education, outreach, research or placements, and make sure they are told about the learned societies and professional bodies relevant to them.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider to inform students and offer opportunities

statements.paraphrase: A provider's assessment strategy will mirror the skills and understanding the curriculum builds, aligned with the course's teaching and learning at course and module level; it will follow the stated learning outcomes, support learning and let students show progressing attainment, so that assessment for and as learning is fostered.

forPractitioner.text: Set an assessment strategy aligned with teaching and learning at course and module level, tied directly to the learning outcomes, supporting learning and letting students show attainment that grows over the course, so that assessment serves learning, not only measurement.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider in setting assessment strategy

statements.paraphrase: Law assessment will use a mix of methods accessible to every student; providers can make inclusive, authentic strategies transparent to prevent disadvantage, and where a method disadvantages a student, adjustments will be considered with that student, keeping the whole cohort fair.

forPractitioner.text: Use a mix of assessment methods that all students can access, be open about inclusive and authentic strategies, and where a method disadvantages an individual, consider adjustments with that student while keeping fairness for the cohort.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider; the student takes part in discussing adjustments but does not carry the duty

statements.about: a range of assessment and the overall burden
statements.paraphrase: Law students will meet a range of assessment methods; assessment that identifies diverse learner needs will be told apart from assessment of later academic performance, and providers will design assessment with the overall load, wellbeing and accessibility in mind.

forPractitioner.text: Give students a range of assessment methods, distinguish assessment that identifies learners' needs from assessment of their later performance, and design the whole assessment load with wellbeing and accessibility in view.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider in designing assessment

statements.paraphrase: Students will receive feedback on formative and summative work that lets them carry it forward into later assessments; providers may build feedback literacy and self-efficacy through peer and self-assessment, marking criteria and exemplars, and could use varied feedback formats for equality and inclusion.

forPractitioner.text: Give feedback on formative and summative work that students can act on in later assessments; consider peer and self-assessment, work with marking criteria and exemplars to build feedback literacy, and vary feedback formats, written, audio, screencast or oral, for inclusion.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider to give feedback; the student uses it (see 4.4.b15)

statements.appliesTo: higher education providers awarding honours degrees in Law
statements.about: performance above the threshold: Annex D
statements.paraphrase: Most students will do considerably better than the minimum; each provider decides what evidence shows this and should refer to Annex D, which describes the four honours classes (1st, 2.1, 2.2, 3rd) at FHEQ level 6 and FQHEIS level 10.

forPractitioner.text: Above the threshold, judge achievement by your own method and refer to Annex D's descriptions of the four honours classes; this statement gives no typical or excellent lists of its own.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the awarding body for judging classes above the threshold

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.paraphrase: Find and obtain standard legal materials for the relevant jurisdictions, in print and online.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates find, locate and retrieve standard legal materials in print and electronic form for the jurisdictions they study.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation you should be able to find and obtain the standard legal materials for the jurisdictions you study, in print and online.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.about: synthesising primary and secondary legal sources
statements.paraphrase: Bring together information from several primary and secondary legal sources, judge their relative weight and so gain knowledge and understanding of complex legal issues.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates combine primary and secondary legal sources, weigh their relative value and reach an understanding of complex legal issues.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation you should be able to combine information from primary and secondary legal sources, judge how much weight each carries and use them to understand complex legal issues.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.paraphrase: Apply legal knowledge to problem scenarios and reach reasoned conclusions backed by legal authority.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates use their legal knowledge on problem questions and reach conclusions reasoned from legal authority.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation you should be able to use your legal knowledge on problem questions and reach conclusions you can support with legal authority.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.about: possible outcomes grounded in authority and research
statements.paraphrase: Set out several possible outcomes to a problem, grounded in legal authority and drawing on current research and advanced scholarship.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates map out several possible outcomes to a problem, each grounded in authority and drawing on current research and scholarship.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation you should be able to set out several possible outcomes to a legal problem, each backed by authority and by current research and scholarship.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.paraphrase: Judge critically how strong particular arguments are and choose between alternative solutions with reasons.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates critically weigh the merits of arguments and choose, with reasons, between competing solutions.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation you should be able to judge critically how strong an argument is and choose between different solutions, giving your reasons.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.paraphrase: Show suitable legal citation and reasoning in written work and communication.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates cite legal authority correctly and reason soundly in writing and other communication.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation you should be able to cite legal sources correctly and reason clearly in your writing and other work.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.paraphrase: Analyse, evaluate and interpret the primary materials of law, such as statutes, law reports, treaties and directives.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates analyse, assess and interpret statutes, law reports, treaties, directives and other primary legal materials.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation you should be able to analyse, assess and interpret primary legal materials such as statutes, law reports, treaties and directives.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.paraphrase: Understand and use legal terminology, in speech, other forms and writing, to put across and explain technical legal information.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates understand legal terms and use them, orally, in writing and in other forms, to convey technical legal points.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation you should be able to understand legal terms and use them in speech and writing to explain technical legal points.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.about: legal research techniques, including from other disciplines
statements.paraphrase: Show a range of legal research techniques, drawing where suitable on methods from other humanities and social science disciplines.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates use several techniques of legal research, including, where it fits, methods borrowed from the humanities and social sciences.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation you should be able to use several legal research techniques, including methods from other humanities and social science subjects where they help.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.about: uncertainty and the limits of knowledge in law
statements.paraphrase: Show some awareness of the uncertainties, ambiguities and limits of knowledge built into law and how they affect understanding and applying it.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates show some awareness that law carries uncertainty, ambiguity and limits to knowledge, and how these shape its understanding and use.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation you should be able to show some awareness that law is often uncertain or ambiguous, and how that affects how it is understood and applied.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.paraphrase: Show understanding of law in its many settings, from the individual to the global, and in its institutional, normative, economic, political, social, cultural, historical, ethical, ecological, technological and philosophical dimensions.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates show they understand law across settings from local to global and across its wider dimensions, such as social, economic, ethical and ecological.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation you should be able to show that you understand law in settings from the personal to the global and in its wider dimensions, such as social, economic, ethical and environmental.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.about: legal skills for reaching unfamiliar branches of law
statements.paraphrase: Show a range of legal skills, such as critical analysis and problem-solving, enough to reach a basic grasp of any branch of the relevant jurisdictions, including ones not yet studied.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates have legal skills, such as critical analysis and problem-solving, that let them gain a basic grasp of any branch of law in their jurisdictions, studied or not.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation you should be able to use legal skills such as critical analysis and problem-solving to get a basic grasp of any area of law, even one you have not studied.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.paraphrase: Build digital literacy for finding, organising, creating and sharing information.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates have built digital literacy in locating, managing, producing and sharing information.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation you should be able to use digital skills to find, organise, create and share information.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.paraphrase: Take part in problem-solving exercises.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates have taken part in problem-solving exercises.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation you should be able to take part in problem-solving exercises.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.paraphrase: Build employability skills and awareness of careers, professional requirements and the need to plan ahead.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates have built employability skills and know about career options, professional requirements and the value of planning.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation you should be able to show employability skills and know about your career options, the professional requirements that apply and why you need to plan ahead.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.paraphrase: Become aware of where the legal profession is heading and how it keeps changing.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates are aware of the direction of the legal profession and of its continual change.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation you should be aware of where the legal profession is heading and how it keeps changing.

headingPath: Threshold level: Generic skills and qualities of mind

statements.paraphrase: Pick out the issues, questions and problems in a situation.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates spot the issues, questions and problems a situation raises.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation you should be able to spot the issues, questions and problems in a situation.

headingPath: Threshold level: Generic skills and qualities of mind

statements.paraphrase: Recognise what they do not yet know and learn it.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates recognise the gaps in their knowledge and fill them.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation you should be able to see what you do not yet know and go and learn it.

headingPath: Threshold level: Generic skills and qualities of mind

statements.paraphrase: Grasp and break down knowledge and information.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates make sense of knowledge and information and analyse it.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation you should be able to make sense of information and analyse it.

headingPath: Threshold level: Generic skills and qualities of mind

statements.paraphrase: Draw together what is known on a given topic.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates synthesise current knowledge on a topic.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation you should be able to bring together what is known about a topic.

headingPath: Threshold level: Generic skills and qualities of mind

statements.paraphrase: Use knowledge and understanding to reach evidenced conclusions, including on complex real or hypothetical problems.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates apply what they know to reach evidenced conclusions, including on complex real or imagined problems.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation you should be able to use what you know to reach conclusions backed by evidence, including on complex real or imagined problems.

headingPath: Threshold level: Generic skills and qualities of mind

statements.paraphrase: Communicate effectively and suitably, in speech or in other forms.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates communicate effectively and appropriately, orally or otherwise.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation you should be able to communicate clearly and appropriately, in speech or in other ways.

headingPath: Threshold level: Generic skills and qualities of mind

statements.paraphrase: Present knowledge or an argument so that others can follow it.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates present knowledge or argument in a form others can understand.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation you should be able to present knowledge or an argument so others can follow it.

headingPath: Threshold level: Generic skills and qualities of mind

statements.about: working with qualitative and quantitative data
statements.paraphrase: Handle varied data, including qualitative and quantitative empirical data.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates work with a range of data, qualitative and quantitative.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation you should be able to work with different kinds of data, including qualitative and quantitative evidence.

headingPath: Threshold level: Generic skills and qualities of mind

statements.paraphrase: Use varied digital technologies to gather, analyse, select and present information.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates use different digital technologies to gather, analyse, choose and present information.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation you should be able to use different digital tools to gather, analyse, choose and present information.

headingPath: Threshold level: Generic skills and qualities of mind

statements.paraphrase: Show intellectual independence: work on tasks alone with suitable guidance and support, carry out self-directed research and judge critically.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates work independently with fitting support, direct their own research and exercise critical judgement.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation you should be able to work on your own, with the right guidance, direct your own research and make critical judgements.

headingPath: Threshold level: Generic skills and qualities of mind

statements.paraphrase: Work with others, in a group or team or by taking part in discussion.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates collaborate in groups or teams and contribute to discussion.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation you should be able to work with others in a group or team and take part in discussion.

headingPath: Threshold level: Generic skills and qualities of mind

statements.about: reflection on progress and academic integrity
statements.paraphrase: Reflect on their own progress, including matters of academic integrity.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates reflect on their progress, taking in questions of integrity in their academic work.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation you should be able to reflect on your own progress, including how you keep your work honest and properly referenced.

headingPath: Threshold level: Generic skills and qualities of mind

statements.about: values and ethics in law, society and the self
statements.paraphrase: Identify and examine the values and ethics underlying law, culture and society, and their own.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates examine the values and ethics beneath law, culture and society and in their own lives.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation you should be able to identify and question the values and ethics behind law, culture and society, and your own.

headingPath: Threshold level: Generic skills and qualities of mind

statements.paraphrase: Understand why well-being, mental health and emotions matter and how they bear on learning.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates understand how well-being, mental health and emotion relate to learning.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation you should understand why your well-being, mental health and emotions matter and how they affect your learning.

headingPath: Threshold level: Generic skills and qualities of mind

statements.paraphrase: Make good use of feedback to advance their intellectual development.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates use the feedback they receive to develop intellectually.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation you should be able to use the feedback you get to develop your thinking.

headingPath: Threshold level: Generic skills and qualities of mind

statements.about: contemporary debates on law and society
statements.paraphrase: Appreciate and join current debates on law, individuals, culture and society, such as inequality and sustainability.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates follow and take part in current debates on law and society, for example on inequality and sustainability.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation you should be able to follow and take part in current debates about law and society, such as on inequality and sustainability.
